title: Quantitative torsion reflection for a fixed compatible algebraization
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], $M$ a coherent $I$-adic system, $N$ a coherent $K$-adic system [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $H$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. For every $q\geq1$ and every Noetherian instance on $V(K^q)$, assume completion with respect to the extended ideal $I\mathcal O_{V(K^q)}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an equivalence. Supply $\alpha:M\to\widehat H_I$, $\delta:N\to\widehat H_K$, and natural isomorphisms $\theta_{e,n}:(H/K^{e+1}H)/I^{n+1}\cong(H/I^{n+1}H)/K^{e+1}$ and $\sigma_{e,n}:N_e/I^{n+1}N_e\cong M_n/K^{e+1}M_n$. Assume $\sigma_{e,n}$ followed by $\alpha_n$ modulo $K^{e+1}$ equals $\delta_e$ modulo $I^{n+1}$ followed by $\theta_{e,n}$ for every $e,n\geq0$. If $t\geq1$ and $K^t$ annihilates the ordinary sheaf kernels and cokernels of every $\alpha_n$, then $K^{4t}$ annihilates the ordinary sheaf kernels and cokernels of every $\delta_e$. The systems and morphisms are fixed inputs; this statement has no existence conclusion and imposes no quotient-projection condition on $\theta$.

proof.text: On affine sections, apply the scalar quasi-inverse and reduction assertion of Remark 0888 to each alpha_n with J=K^(e+1). The two scalar composites survive reduction, so K^(2t) kills the reduced kernel and cokernel. Local checking of ideal products gives the same sheaf-level bound. The square and invertibility of sigma and theta identify these maps with the components of completion_I(delta_e).

Both coherent terms of delta_e are killed by K^(e+1), so descend the map to Z_e by the closed-immersion equivalence. The component K^(2t) bound yields the bound K^(4t) on its formal kernel and cokernel: the canonical reverse maps for pairs of scalars in K^(2t) are natural under reduction; their inverse limits retain both scalar composite identities. On each affine open these identities kill the kernel and cokernel of the completed map by K^(4t).

Completion on Z_e is an equivalence, hence exact and reflects zero. Write the coherent ideal product as the image of the ideal-action map J tensor P to P, for J the image of K^(4t) and P the coherent kernel or cokernel. On affine opens, completion of finite modules over a Noetherian ring is tensoring with its flat completed ring, so it preserves this image and its multiplication map. The preceding completed bound therefore makes the formal completion of each coherent product zero. The global completion equivalence on Z_e reflects this zero object, without assuming affine completion is faithful. Closed pushforward and its ideal-product comparison identify the resulting zero products with the claimed products on X. The exponent is independent of e; no new algebraization is chosen.

theorem grothendieckDevissage_secondAdicSystem_torsion
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (M : CoherentFormalModule X I)
    (hthick : ∀ (e : ℕ), 1 ≤ e →
      ∀ (hZ : IsNoetherian (K ^ e).subscheme),
        Functor.IsEquivalence
          (@completion ((K ^ e).subscheme) hZ (I.comap (K ^ e).subschemeι)))
    (H : CoherentModules X) (α : M ⟶ (completion X I).obj H)
    (θ : formalCompletionSystem K H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅
      (formalCompletionSystem I H.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip)
    (N : CoherentFormalModule X K) (δ : N ⟶ (completion X K).obj H)
    (σ : N.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor I ≅
      (M.obj ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor K).flip)
    (hsquare : ∀ e n : ℕ,
        (σ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n) ≫
          formalModuleQuotientMap K (α.hom.app (op n)) (Nat.le_refl (e + 1)) =
        formalModuleQuotientMap I (δ.hom.app (op e)) (Nat.le_refl (n + 1)) ≫
          (θ.hom.app (op e)).app (op n))
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (hα : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) :
    ∀ e : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι (4 * t)).2
        (kernel (δ.hom.app (op e)))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι (4 * t)).2
        (cokernel (δ.hom.app (op e))))
